entities.summary:
Macías was a Galician troubadour and one of the last Galician medieval poets.

Born in medieval Galicia, Macías' life and works are closely tied to the cultural and linguistic landscape of the region.

Macías was a key figure in the transmission of Galician poetry, contributing to the preservation of the region's unique literary heritage.

The loss of Macías and his contemporaries marked the end of a golden age in Galician literature, leaving behind a legacy of poetry that would influence future generations.

In 1401, Macías' death was a poignant reminder of the transience of artistic and cultural achievements, a phenomenon that would continue to resonate throughout European history.

entities.summary:
Macías was a Galician troubadour and one of the last Galician medieval poets.
He was born in 1401 in Galicia, Spain, to a noble family and began his poetic career at a young age, drawing inspiration from the works of earlier Galician poets such as Martín Codax and Pero López de Rueda. His poetry is characterized by its use of the galician-portuguese language and its exploration of themes related to love, nature, and social justice.
Macías' work had a lasting impact on the development of Galician literature, influencing generations of poets and writers who followed in his footsteps. He died in 1401, at the age of 0, leaving behind a body of work that is still studied and admired today for its beauty, depth, and historical significance.
Macías' legacy can be seen in the many festivals and celebrations held in Galicia every year to honor his memory and celebrate the rich cultural heritage of the region.
